title: Sykes–Picot Agreement
summary: In 1916 Britain and France, represented by Mark Sykes and François Georges-Picot, secretly agreed how to divide Ottoman territory in the Middle East between themselves. The final terms were exchanged on 9 and 16 May 1916, after Russia consented. The text set French and British zones of control and an international zone for Palestine.

uncertainty.note: Final terms sent 9 May and ratified 16 May 1916 per The National Archives. The same blog dates the Sykes–Picot deal to 3 February 1916; other accounts differ, so the record uses the year.

where.historical_name: London, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

importance.justification: Secret wartime plan to partition the Ottoman Arab provinces, still widely cited as a source of later Middle East disputes.

sources.title: ‘Dividing the bear’s skin while the bear is still alive’

reviewer_note: Pin is London as a proxy (the Anglo-French talks met there; no single signing site). Sources differ on the date of the Sykes–Picot deal; the year is safe, the day is not.
